assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
caveats: Duplicate records on 12 Oct: 341 attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts, +3.0%). Paysight counts each attempt once and removed the duplicates, keeping the first ingestion.

Volume spike 18 Oct–31 Oct: attempt volume was about 39% above the usual level for those weekdays. Sales and data gaps both look like this, so check before comparing totals across this period. It is not a data error by itself and is flagged for context.
Success rate depends on the denominator: 82.69% at attempt level, 84.49% at order level and 85.09% technical. Retries and drop-offs explain the gap.

facts.text: Debit card attempt success rate fell 3.32pp, from 86.01% (24,000 attempts) in 10–20 Oct to 82.69% (29,554 attempts) in 21–31 Oct. The change is statistically and practically significant.
Split by issuer, the change is almost entirely a within-issuer rate effect (-3.29pp), with a negligible mix effect (-0.03pp). Issuer shares barely moved.

Harbor Bank is about a quarter of debit volume but accounts for -2.88pp (about 87%) of the -3.32pp change. Its success rate fell 11.33pp, from 85.87% to 74.55%, and the drop is statistically significant.
The other five issuers moved little: Banyan Bank fell 1.30pp, Ridge Bank 0.94pp, Coral Bank 0.77pp, Indigo Bank 0.16pp and Lotus Bank 0.02pp. None of these is statistically significant.

For Harbor Bank debit, ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE rose from 0.45 to 13.96 per 100 attempts (1,052 failures in the current period vs 27 in the baseline), an increase of 13.51 per 100 attempts. No other failure code moved by more than 0.72 per 100 attempts.
Across all debit cards, ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE rose from 0.41 to 3.86 per 100 attempts (1,142 failures in the current period vs 98). Other codes were roughly flat.
Harbor Bank's daily success rate was 83.7–88.9% through 20 Oct, then 73.31% on 21 Oct, the first day of the current period.
All four acquirers show a similar fall of 2.94pp to 3.50pp, so the drop is not tied to one acquirer.
Success rate depends on the denominator. For 21–31 Oct it is 82.69% at attempt level, 84.49% at order level and 85.09% on a technical basis.

response.headline: Debit card success rate fell 3.32pp, from 86.0% to 82.7%, and almost all of it is a like-for-like drop rather than a change in mix. Harbor Bank debit cards alone account for about 2.88pp of the fall, driven by a jump in issuer risk declines.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Ask Harbor Bank whether risk or fraud rules, scoring thresholds or BIN-level controls changed on or about 21 Oct. Check whether declined attempts share common traits such as ticket size, channel or merchant category.
hypotheses.rationale: The decline is concentrated in one issuer, starts abruptly on 21 Oct, and is explained almost entirely by the ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE code, which rose from 0.45 to 13.96 per 100 attempts. Other decline types did not rise.
hypotheses.text: Harbor Bank (or its risk engine) tightened fraud or risk rules around 21 Oct, causing a surge in risk declines on its debit cards.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Compare Harbor Bank's risk-decline rate by hour and by merchant on 18–21 Oct against transaction counts and amounts.
hypotheses.rationale: Attempt volume was about 39% above the usual level from 18 Oct. However, Harbor Bank's rate was still 84.1% and 83.7% on 18–19 Oct, so volume alone does not explain the abrupt fall on 21 Oct.
hypotheses.text: The rise in risk declines is linked to the higher attempt volume seen in this period, for example a sale triggering velocity or fraud checks at Harbor Bank.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Harbor Bank is about a quarter of debit volume but accounts for -2.88pp (about 87%) of the -3.32pp change.
recommendations.rationale: This single segment explains about 87% of the fall, and the failure-code shift points to risk declines.
recommendations.text: Raise the Harbor Bank debit ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE spike with the issuer or acquirer and request a review of any risk-rule change from 21 Oct.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Harbor Bank's daily success rate was 83.7–88.9% through 20 Oct, then 73.31% on 21 Oct.
recommendations.rationale: The shift is abrupt and concentrated, so a daily alert would catch a recurrence or a reversal quickly.
recommendations.text: Monitor Harbor Bank debit success rate and risk-decline share daily until it returns to about 85–86%, and set an alert on that code.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Harbor Bank debit risk-decline hypothesis (tightened rules around 21 Oct).
recommendations.rationale: If these declines are false positives, recovering them would restore a meaningful part of the lost success rate.
recommendations.text: Review the affected declined Harbor Bank attempts for legitimate customers, and consider a retry or alternative payment method flow for risk-declined debit payments.
